title: Composing MIDI Tricks
intro: Getting ideas out of your head and into the sequencer before they evaporate. These tricks are about speed of capture first and correctness second — you can always fix it later, but you cannot un‑forget an idea.

tips.t: Capture the last thing you played, even when not recording
tips.d: If you played something great without recording, press ⇧R (Flashback Capture) and Logic turns it into a region. MIDI can be captured whether the project is playing or stopped. Audio capture arrived in Logic 11.2: give the audio track focus and play the project. Logic saves audio only while there is an incoming signal, needs at least four seconds of playback, and keeps up to one minute.

tips.t: Use the Step Input Keyboard for parts you cannot play
tips.d: Choose Window > Show Step Input Keyboard to enter notes one at a time, setting each note's length and velocity with the Note Length and Velocity buttons.

src.label: Apple — Use step input recording techniques in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Draw notes with the Pencil, delete with the Eraser
tips.d: The Pencil creates a note whose length, velocity and MIDI channel match the last note you created or edited. To remove a note, select it and press Delete, or click it with the Eraser tool. ⌥-drag a note to copy it to a new position.

src.label: Apple — Add notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Delete notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Copy notes in the Piano Roll Editor in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use the Chord Trigger MIDI plugin to play chords with one finger
tips.d: Insert Chord Trigger in the MIDI FX slot and click Learn. Click the trigger key you want on the upper keyboard first, then click the notes of the chord on the lower keyboard, then click Learn again to finish. Whole progressions become one-finger performances.

src.label: Apple — Use Chord Trigger in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Chord Trigger overview in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Force everything into key with Transposer
tips.d: Insert the Transposer MIDI FX and set its Root and Scale pop-up menus. Transposer transposes incoming MIDI notes in real time and corrects them to the selected scale, so you stay in key as you play. Choose User and click notes off on the on-screen keyboard to build your own scale.

src.label: Apple — Transposer in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use Arpeggiator to generate parts, then commit them
tips.d: Insert Arpeggiator and dial in a pattern, then commit it with Bounce in Place. Logic renders the selected region, including all active plug-ins and automation data, to a 24-bit audio file at the project sample rate. The live pattern becomes a fixed part you can edit as audio.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro for Mac bounce in place overview

tips.d: Select the regions and change Transpose in the Region inspector. Region parameters affect how regions play back but don't alter the data inside them, and every selected region changes together. If the project is playing, you hear the change immediately, so you can audition a new key and set it back to zero if it doesn't work.

tips.t: Use the Modifier MIDI plugin to reassign a controller
tips.d: The Modifier MIDI plug-in reassigns or filters a single continuous controller or fader event. Choose or learn the incoming type in Input Event and the outgoing type in Re-Assign To, then use the Scale and Add sliders to scale or offset the output values.

src.label: Apple — Modifier in Logic Pro for Mac

groups.heading: Working fast while ideas are hot

tips.t: Merge takes when you are layering, not replacing
tips.d: For building up a drum pattern one element per pass, set MIDI cycle recording to Merge instead. Each loop adds to the same region.

src.label: Apple — Recording settings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Freeze the instrument as soon as the part is done
tips.d: Freeze the software instrument track once the part is done. Logic renders its instrument and effect plug-ins so they stop costing CPU, and unlike Bounce in Place, Freeze lets you return to the original track and its automation more easily.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro for Mac bounce in place overview
Apple — Freeze tracks in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

tips.t: Commit a MIDI region to audio with Bounce in Place
tips.d: Select the MIDI region and use Bounce in Place. Logic renders it through the instrument and all active plug-ins, plus automation data, to a 24-bit audio region at the project sample rate, which locks the idea in as audio.

src.label: Apple — Logic Pro for Mac bounce in place overview
Apple — Bounce regions in place in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Keep one “sketch” instrument track loaded at all times
tips.d: Keep a piano patch on a permanently armed track so any idea can be captured right away. The moment capture takes effort, ideas stop arriving.

tips.t: Use Note Repeat for hi‑hats and rolls
tips.d: In Step Sequencer, choose Note Repeat from the Edit Mode selector, then drag up on a hi-hat step to slice it into more repeats (1 to 16) or down for fewer. The inspector adds velocity ramp, velocity curve and Distribution for each step, so a roll can accelerate or decelerate instead of sitting flat.
